### A classical assessment {#projects-exam}

The official mode combines homework, quizzes and team projects, so this proposal keeps all three and gives the team project the largest weight, in the seminar format of chapter 2. All weights are ours.

| Component | Weight | Format | Covers |
|---|---|---|---|
| Homework | 20 % | Ex. 2, Ex. 7 and Ex. 10, and the session-7 Fourier-feature lab notebook, 5 % each | ch. 4, 6, 9, 10.1 |
| Quizzes | 20 % | two closed-book quizzes of 20 minutes, in sessions 5 and 8, 10 % each | ch. 1, 3–6 (quiz 1); ch. 7–9, 10.1–10.2 (quiz 2) |
| Team project: paper presentation | 20 % | teams of 3–4; 20 minutes and 10 minutes of questions, with the grid of section 2.1 | one paper of the list of section 2.1 |
| Team project: replication report | 30 % | 6–8 pages and a repository (section 2.3), protocol of definition 1.1 | ch. 1–2 and the chapter of the paper |
| Team project: defense | 10 % | 15 minutes in session 9, with individual questions | the replication |

**Resit.** An individual oral of 30 minutes: questions on the team's replication and on one paper of the section 2.1 list, drawn at the start of the oral.

**Sample questions.** Five questions of 4 points (20 in total), of the kind the two quizzes would draw from; together they make a mock paper of about 60 minutes.

**Q1 (4 pts) — A separable convolution, counted.** A $3 \times 3$ convolution maps $128$ channels to $128$ channels on a $56 \times 56$ feature map. Count its multiply-accumulates (MACs), then those of its depthwise separable version (proposition 3.1), and compare their ratio with the key result of section 3.1.

::: proof
[Marking points]{.tag}

-   Standard convolution:
    $$
    56 \cdot 56 \cdot 9 \cdot 128 \cdot 128 \approx 4.62 \times 10^8 \ \text{MACs}
    $$
    (1 pt).
-   Separable version: the depthwise part costs $56 \cdot 56 \cdot 9 \cdot 128 \approx 3.6 \times 10^6$ and the pointwise part $56 \cdot 56 \cdot 128^2 \approx 5.14 \times 10^7$, about $5.50 \times 10^7$ in total (1.5 pts).
-   Ratio $\approx 0.119$, equal to $1/128 + 1/9$ (1 pt).
-   The pointwise part is $93\,\%$ of the cost, and the ratio tends to $1/k^2 \approx 0.11$ as the width grows: shrinking the kernel further barely helps (0.5 pt). Common error: counting the depthwise layer as $k^2 d^2$ instead of $k^2 d$.
:::

**Q2 (4 pts) — A gain or noise?** Method A reaches $81.2\,\% \pm 0.8$ and the baseline B $80.1\,\% \pm 0.6$ (mean ± standard deviation over 5 seeds each). Is the difference significant at the 5 % level with a Welch test? What would you check before writing "A beats B"?

::: proof
[Marking points]{.tag}

-   The standard error of the difference is
    $$
    \sqrt{0.8^2/5 + 0.6^2/5} \approx 0.447,
    $$
    so $t \approx 2.46$ (1 pt).
-   The Welch degrees of freedom are about $7.4$, with a critical value of about $2.34$ ($2.31$ with 8 degrees of freedom): significant, $p \approx 0.04$ (1 pt).
-   If the paper makes 20 such comparisons, the Bonferroni threshold $0.05/20 = 0.0025$ makes it non-significant (1 pt).
-   Checks of definition 1.1: same recipe and budget for both methods, seeds that vary every source of randomness, a metric declared before the experiment, the test named in the table (1 pt). Common error: dividing by the standard deviations instead of the standard error, which gives $t \approx 1.1$.
:::

**Q3 (4 pts) — Capacity and cost of a mixture of experts.** A model has 12 MoE layers with $d = 512$, expansion $r = 4$, $E = 8$ experts and top-2 routing. Give the parameters stored in these layers, the parameters active per token and the FLOPs per token (proposition 6.2), and compare with a dense MLP of the same width.

::: proof
[Marking points]{.tag}

-   Stored: $2Erd^2 \approx 16.8$M per layer, about $201$M for the 12 layers (1 pt).
-   Active: $2krd^2 \approx 4.19$M per layer, about $50.3$M in total — the fraction $k/E$ of the stored parameters (1 pt).
-   FLOPs per token: $4krd^2 \approx 8.4$M per layer, about $101$M for the 12 layers, twice a dense MLP of the same width ($4rd^2 \approx 4.2$M per layer) (1 pt).
-   The router costs $2Ed \approx 8 \times 10^3$ FLOPs per layer, which is negligible; memory grows with $E$, compute with $k$ (1 pt). Common error: counting a multiply-add as one FLOP, whereas proposition 6.2 counts two.
:::

**Q4 (4 pts) — Compute-optimal allocation.** Minimize the loss of definition 9.1 under the budget $6ND = C$ and show that the optimal model size grows as
$$
N^\star \propto C^{\beta/(\alpha+\beta)} .
$$
With $\alpha = 0.34$ and $\beta = 0.28$, by how much should $N$ and $D$ grow when the compute budget is multiplied by 10?

::: proof
[Marking points]{.tag}

-   Substitute $D = C/(6N)$ and set the derivative in $N$ to zero:
    $$
    \alpha A\,N^{-\alpha-1} = \beta B\,(6/C)^{\beta}\,N^{\beta-1}, \quad\text{so}\quad N^{\alpha+\beta} = \frac{\alpha A}{\beta B}\Big(\frac{C}{6}\Big)^{\beta}
    $$
    (1.5 pts).
-   Hence $N^\star \propto C^{\beta/(\alpha+\beta)}$ and, since $D^\star = C/(6N^\star)$, also $D^\star \propto C^{\alpha/(\alpha+\beta)}$ (1 pt).
-   The exponents are $0.45$ and $0.55$: $N$ grows by $10^{0.45} \approx 2.8$ and $D$ by $10^{0.55} \approx 3.5$ (1 pt).
-   Tokens per parameter grow by $10^{0.10} \approx 1.25$ per decade of compute, close to the constant ratio of the symmetric case of theorem 9.2 (0.5 pt). Common error: attributing this additive law to Kaplan et al. (2020) instead of Hoffmann et al. (2022).
:::

**Q5 (4 pts) — Reading a results table.** A paper reports "ViT-X: 82.4 % top-1 on ImageNet, against 79.0 % for ResNet-50". ViT-X was trained for 300 epochs with AdamW, RandAugment and mixup, on one seed; the ResNet-50 figure is copied from an older paper (90 epochs, SGD, basic augmentation). Name the flaws with the grid of definition 1.1, say how much of the gap the recipe alone could explain, and propose a fair experiment.

::: proof
[Marking points]{.tag}

-   Unequal recipes and budgets: the baseline was not retrained under the same conditions (1 pt).
-   One seed: no variance is reported, so no test is possible (1 pt).
-   The first line of the ConvNeXt table (chapter 5): the modern recipe alone takes a ResNet from 76.1 to 78.8, so most of the 3.4-point gap may be the recipe (1 pt).
-   A fair protocol: retrain ResNet-50 with the same recipe and number of epochs, at least 3 seeds per model, mean ± standard deviation with a named test, and FLOPs or throughput reported (1 pt). Common error: answering "ViT needs more data", which is true (note on the ViT paper) but is not a flaw of this comparison.
:::

### Projects {#projects-list}

Every project uses public data and runs on a laptop CPU or one free Colab T4 GPU, with only this module and Deep Learning (P1). Levels ★/★★/★★★ are those of the exercises, and efforts are per student; the group card is a candidate topic for the official team project, and the solo cards can serve as homework extensions, resit topics, or be merged by a team into one study.

**Grading grid used by every project of this page** (a project card may replace one row).

| Criterion | Weight |
|---|---|
| Question and success metric stated before the experiments | 10 % |
| Correct use of the course results (cited by number) | 25 % |
| Protocol: leakage-free split, baselines, at least 3 seeds, intervals | 25 % |
| Results and analysis: error analysis, limits, one responsible-AI remark | 20 % |
| Reproducibility: repository, README, pinned environment, one command | 10 % |
| Communication: report (≤ 6 pages solo, ≤ 10 group) or 10-minute oral | 10 % |

Group projects: a contribution statement and an oral with individual questions; the individual grade is the group grade times a factor in [0.8, 1.2].

#### P1 · ★★ · solo · Label-efficient transfer on satellite images {#proj-1}

| Field | Content |
|---|---|
| Goal | Compare CLIP zero-shot classification, a linear probe on frozen DINOv2 features and a fine-tuned supervised ResNet-18 with 1 %, 10 % and 100 % of the EuroSAT training labels; report accuracy with 95 % intervals over 5 seeds, Welch tests against the supervised baseline, and the label fraction at which the probe overtakes it. |
| Data | [EuroSAT (RGB)](https://zenodo.org/records/7711810) — MIT licence — 27,000 Sentinel-2 images of 64 × 64 pixels in 10 land-use classes, 95 MB; loading: `torchvision.datasets.EuroSAT(root, download=True)` |
| Chapters | [ch. 1](#ch1) (definition 1.1, example 1.2), [ch. 4](#ch4) (ViT), 7.2 (CLIP), 8.2 (DINOv2); [Deep Learning ch. 4](../m1p1-deep-learning/index.html#ch4) and [ch. 7](../m1p1-deep-learning/index.html#ch7) (ResNet, fine-tuning) |
| Deliverables | notebook and 4-page report |
| Effort and compute | ≈ 18 h per student · one free Colab T4: feature extraction ≈ 10 min per backbone, each ResNet-18 run ≤ 15 min |
| Objectives served | O5 (vision–language models), O6 (environment and public institutions: land use), O9 (replication protocol) |
| Specific criterion | Replaces the Protocol row (25 %): label subsets stratified, fixed per seed and shared by the three methods; the test split (20 %) touched once, at the end |
| Going further | Few-shot prompt ensembles for CLIP, or the 13-band multispectral version (2 GB) with an adapted first layer. |

#### P2 · ★★ · solo · A mixture-of-experts character model {#proj-2}

| Field | Content |
|---|---|
| Goal | Train a 4-layer character-level transformer on Tiny Shakespeare with dense MLPs, then with MoE layers (definition 6.1: $E = 4$ or $8$, top-2, capacity factor 1.0 or 1.25, auxiliary loss on or off); report validation bits per character against the dense model at equal active FLOPs, the coefficient of variation of the routed fractions $f_i$, and Ex. 7 answered on measured routings, over 3 seeds. |
| Data | [Tiny Shakespeare](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/karpathy/char-rnn/master/data/tinyshakespeare/input.txt) — public-domain text (repository under MIT licence) — 1.1 MB, 65 distinct characters; loading: `urllib.request.urlretrieve(url, "input.txt")`, split 90 / 10 by position |
| Chapters | [ch. 6](#ch6) (definition 6.1, proposition 6.2, load-balancing loss, Ex. 7), [ch. 9](#ch9) (9.1 recipe), [ch. 1](#ch1) (seeds); [Deep Learning ch. 6](../m1p1-deep-learning/index.html#ch6) (transformer) |
| Deliverables | notebook and 4-page report |
| Effort and compute | ≈ 20 h per student · one T4; each run ≤ 5 min ($d = 256$, context 256, 5,000 steps), about 30 runs |
| Objectives served | O3 (LLM architecture: sparse experts), O1 (foundations: capacity versus compute) |
| Going further | Balancing without an auxiliary loss, by a per-expert bias on the router logits, or the first 10 MB of enwik8 for a larger alphabet. |

#### P3 · ★★ · solo · Physics-informed network, Fourier features or emulator? {#proj-3}

| Field | Content |
|---|---|
| Goal | On the 1D viscous Burgers equation, compare a physics-informed network (definition 10.9, the baseline), the same network with Fourier-feature inputs (10.1) and an emulator trained once on simulated trajectories; report the relative $L^2$ error at the final time on 10 held-out initial conditions (100 for the emulator) against the GPU-minutes of training. |
| Data | [PDEBench, 1D Burgers, ν = 0.01](https://darus.uni-stuttgart.de/dataset.xhtml?persistentId=doi:10.18419/darus-2986) — CC BY 4.0 — one HDF5 file of 8.2 GB holding 10,000 trajectories on 1,024 points and 201 times; loading: `h5py.File("1D_Burgers_Sols_Nu0.01.hdf5")["tensor"][:2000, ::4, ::4]` (2,000 trajectories on a coarser grid) |
| Chapters | [ch. 10](#ch10): 10.1 (Fourier features), 10.3 (amortization), 10.5 (definition 10.9, example 10.10); [ch. 1](#ch1) (protocol) |
| Deliverables | notebook and 4-page report |
| Effort and compute | ≈ 22 h per student · one T4; one PINN fit ≈ 5–10 min per initial condition, the emulator (an MLP or a 1D CNN on 256 points) ≈ 20 min |
| Objectives served | O1 (foundations: inductive bias and optimization), O9 (research readiness: physics-informed learning) |
| Specific criterion | Replaces the Protocol row (25 %): equal wall-clock budgets, the PINN's cost counted per initial condition and the emulator's once (amortization, 10.3), 3 seeds |
| Going further | A Fourier neural operator on the same file, or the file with ν = 0.001, where plain PINNs are known to struggle. |

#### P4 · ★★★ · group · Self-supervised pre-training for histopathology {#proj-4}

| Field | Content |
|---|---|
| Goal | Pre-train a ResNet-18 with SimCLR (chapter 7) and a small ViT with MAE (chapter 8) on 50,000 unlabelled PatchCamelyon patches, then fit linear probes with 1 % and 10 % of the labels; report test AUROC and accuracy with 95 % intervals over 3 seeds, against a supervised ResNet-18 trained from scratch on the same labels and an ImageNet-pretrained one. |
| Data | [PatchCamelyon (PCam)](https://zenodo.org/records/2546921) — MIT licence on the Zenodo record; patches cut from the Camelyon16 lymph-node slides — 327,680 patches of 96 × 96 pixels with a binary tumour label, 6.4 GB for the training images; loading: `h5py.File("camelyonpatch_level_2_split_train_x.h5")["x"][:50000]` after `gunzip` |
| Chapters | [ch. 7](#ch7) (definition 7.1, NT-Xent, proposition 7.3), [ch. 8](#ch8) (definition 8.1, example 8.2), 9.1 (recipe), [ch. 1](#ch1) (protocol); [Deep Learning ch. 4](../m1p1-deep-learning/index.html#ch4) |
| Deliverables | repository with one-command run, 8-page report, 10-minute oral with individual questions |
| Effort and compute | ≈ 30 h per student (3–4 students) · one T4 per student; each pre-training ≤ 2.5 h (100 epochs at 96 × 96 in mixed precision), each probe ≤ 10 min |
| Objectives served | O6 (healthcare: digital pathology), O9 (replication of two papers), O1 (representation learning) |
| Responsible AI | PCam releases no patient metadata, so no subgroup audit is possible: state it as a limitation. The benchmark supports no clinical claim; the 1 % probe models the realistic case of a few annotated slides. |
| Going further | A DINOv2 probe as a strong reference, or stain augmentation and its effect in the 1 % regime. |

### End-of-year projects {#projects-capstone}

No [Year-1 integrative project](../m1-integrative-projects/index.html) requires this option, but two of its chapters serve them. The protocol of chapter 1 (seeds, intervals, Welch tests) strengthens the baseline milestone of every project, and [Y1-7](../m1-integrative-projects/index.html#y1-7) (chest X-rays) can replace its supervised image encoder by a DINOv2 probe or an MAE pre-training (chapter 8).

In Year 2, the equivariance of section 4.4 and the physics-informed losses of section 10.5 feed the force-field capstone [C6](../m2-projet-transverse/index.html#c6), and the robustness of section 4.5 feeds the evasion-attack tests of [C2](../m2-projet-transverse/index.html#c2) (payments compliance).
